summary: "Through My Lens: The Apollo 11 16mm Camera" is an interactive digital storybook that tells the story of the 1969 moon landing through the unique first-person perspective of the Lunar Module's camera. Complete with retro-NASA aesthetics, real mission telemetry, and custom visual diagrams, it blends engineering history with immersive storytelling.
details:
What it does & how it works: An interactive web storybook recounting Apollo 11 from the first-person perspective of the Lunar Module's 16mm camera. Built with HTML/CSS/JS and hosted on GitHub Pages, featuring retro UI, telemetry cards, and shutter audio.

Benefits & Impact: Bridges science communication with creative art, making dense aerospace history emotionally engaging and accessible to all audiences.

Tools used: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (Web Audio API for sound), custom SVG graphics, and GitHub Pages.

Creativity: Uses an objective camera's POV to weave authentic NASA telemetry into an immersive narrative.

Factors considered: Strict historical accuracy and seamless cross-device mobile/desktop UX.
